why: Chad, 13 Nov 2026 (docs/V26.8-E4C3-NOTES.md H, I, K, G): his telling cut to four direct lines, Grandmaster Pho's answer to four (baramee first), one line after the teaching, ending A's line said plainly, ending B's list without shortcuts, and the woman at his bench counting the photograph in. q3t1.prompt: [quiet] Since I was a boy, I have been very sensitive. I feel things other people cannot feel.

q3t2.prompt: [uneasy] When I hear chanting, my body moves by itself, and I cannot control it.

q3t3.prompt: [sincere] When I hold an amulet, I can feel its energy. Every amulet feels different.

q3t4.prompt: [ashamed] And I once kept three kumanthong, and opened my body to them.

ph3n1.prompt: [calm] Every person is born carrying something from past lives. Different people bring different things, and different baramee.

ph3n2.prompt: [warm] You brought yours with you. You were born with a gift, and with a mission.

ph3n3.prompt: [serious] But sensitivity alone is not enough. Without control, it will overwhelm you, and it will hurt you. You opened your body to the kumanthong, and you did not know how to close it.

ph3n4.prompt: [calm] So first, you learn control. To open when you choose, and to close when you choose.

ph3p1.prompt: [calm] Holding it takes years. Then you use it for others, not for yourself.

ph3A2.prompt: [warm] Good. Remember that order when progress is slow. That is when most people give up.

q3B1.prompt: [reluctant] A Sak Yant, for luck. Then another. An amulet shop I kept going back to. Amulets I picked up to see what they would do. Three kumanthong I took home. A master I went to about my business.
